item.title: SCP-XXXX - 4D Pocket
item.description: A pocket which you can pull anything out of. Images are in the works.
item.content:encoded:
Item #: XXXX

Object Class: Safe
Secondary Class: Taumiel
Disruption Class: Vlam
Risk Class: Notice

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is to be kept in High-Value Storage Locker 53D at Site-19 when not being utilized for testing and/or research purposes. The item is safe to handle, and poses no known threats of any kind, though due to its nature, it could be highly powerful depending on the utilization. No human subjects or other SCP's are to be produced out of SCP-XXXX at any time. No personnel with the exception of Class-D personnel with low IQ scores are allowed to enter SCP-XXXX under any circumstance. SCP-XXXX can only be accessed by personnel with level 2 clearance or above, and may occasionally be utilized as a form of additional resources when lack thereof.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a white semi-circle pocket composed of standard rubber. SCP-XXXX is capable of producing any kind of physical object or person a subject desires so long as the said object or person exists and the subject reaches into SCP-XXXX. In order to achieve this, it has been determined that SCP-XXXX can connect with the minds of those who reach in. The size of the objects produced are irrelevant as SCP-XXXX is capable of expanding in size to the exact measurements of the object produced. Objects can also be inserted into SCP-XXXX with minimal struggle.

The quantity of the objects is also irrelevant, as the objects produced are an exact clone of the original copy. Should the original object be specified, it will be produced, though said object will now reside in the location of the production in lieu of its original one. Both SCP-XXXX and the items within remain unaffected by liquids poured inside, though they can be affected upon full production.

SCP-XXXX’s externally measures 8.5 inches in diameter, 4.25 inches in radius, 2 millimeters in thickness, 14 grams in weight, and should two meet, it would have a circumference of approximately 27 inches. SCP-XXXX’s internal measurements are immeasurable. After several tests, it has been determined that SCP-XXXX is 4-Dimensional, causing its internal dimensions and mass to be practically incomprehensible, hence the nickname “4D Pocket”.

SCP-XXXX is also capable of sticking to any solid surface after applying pressure, and can be removed from said surface with ease. To date, SCP-XXXX has shown no other anomalous properties.

« SCP-XXXW | SCP-XXXX | SCP-XXXY »

item.title: Tectonic Watchers
item.description: The unexplained "Earthquake Lights" are actually entities watching these earthquakes.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not until critiqued.

Page Type: SCP Article / Tale.

Genre (Optional): Drama (Possibly something else, but I can't think of what it'd be.)

Page Layout (Optional): It'd begin as a tale. After a medium amount of writing in the tale, it'd then show an entry of the SCP - at least, what is understood about them at that point. Then switching back to tale, then after more is learnt, the document is updated again. Repeat this until the document is fully written, ending with a short note.

Elevator Pitch: An unexplained (yet theorized) scientific phenomena referred to as "Earthquake lights". Strange lights that seem to appear in the skies whilst (usually high-magnitude) earthquakes form. However, what isn't expected is that these are entities made of light, appearing to simply spectate the earthquakes. Why they do this is found out in the tale.

Central Narrative: During a high-magnitude earthquake near Site [REDACTED], there were "Earthquake Lights" spotted by many people. As this is a scientifically unexplained phenomena, MTF Unit Rho-10 "Shaken, Not Stirred" (an MTF unit created to withstand seismic activity, or unnatural geological movement) enters the scene to investigate. After recordings are taken, and the film is placed through numerous filters & analysations, it's found that each of these 'strobes' of light contain a nearly humanoid entity which seems to be watching the earthquakes. When another high-magnitude earthquake occurs near the same area within the next month, the same dispatch is sent to investigate these flashes of light closer. As the protagonist, codename "Charlie-0" (or C-0 by military alphabets) approaches towards the light, it seems to remain still for much longer than previous. They go to the top of the nearest destroyed building via an extremely long grappling hook and a lot of climbing. 23 minutes later, they arrive at the top, before the entity slowly floats down towards him. They take him somewhere - yet to be discovered. The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually. Finally, when he's freed, he decides to watch one final earthquake with them. That's how it'd end, with a full log & a destroyed city.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that this could, hypothetically, be real is a big thing. Playing off of real world unexplained phenomena. Not to mention the fact it opens up as a tale-SCP has always caught my interest. A dangerous scenario (that being an earthquake) being traversed whilst also trying to gain intel on things which you can barely even see for more then a flash of a second is extremely difficult, and thrilling to read about.

Additional Notes: There is almost definitely some shit which I've messed up with the lore, as I am an idiot. Please feel free to be harsh in critique. Thank you!

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137
item.description: Story from the perspective of someone who heard the leaked audio
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: I just listened to TheVolgun’s fantastic audio rendition of SCP-2137 and was very fascinated with the article as a whole.

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

Additional Notes: I’m returning to the SCP wiki after a fairly long absence so I’m sure there are things I’ve missed. I originally formatted this post wrong because last time I posted here no such thing existed. So if this idea has been done, or if it’s very similar to another tale, please let me know!

item.title: Lonely voice
item.description: The voice that speaks to you when you're alone.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fantasy, and Supernatural

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a voice that talks to you when you're alone, separate from any other human contact for a time. It starts as your own thoughts, and diverges from your normal train of thought without your notice. Some people are more inclined to hear it, even when around others, but it talks to anyone separate from humanity for an extended period of time.

Central Narrative: It starts with a psych patient being evaluated for possible anomaly, but a suggestion by one of scientist puts forward the idea that an SCP may be attracted to the situation the patient was in—he had lived alone for many years, secluded. Tests are done putting people in isolation, and many attest to a divergence of thought from their normal thoughts after a time. This is chalked up to normal psychological phenomena, until patterns are seen in the thought patterns: many suggest being drawn away to be separate from humanity, such as going to isolated geographical places, as well as questioning social norms. Several of the test subjects are found to be heading to isolated areas in forests, and atop buildings over following weeks. Basically, the scientists come to the conclusion that the source of the thoughts are voices coming from a variety of non physical beings that dwell in places less inhabited by humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that it's relatable.

Additional Notes: Ehm, as a possible addition to the narrative, these beings are speculated to be aiding it trying to separate humans from each other one by one, as to aid in making an easier invasion of their own species.

item.title: Gossip Ghost
item.description: First Scp - ghost becomes AI, tries to find who they think killed them.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Default, with exposition mostly delivered through fragments on the conversations the program had with its victims.

Elevator Pitch: There's a program in the internet that's going around revealing people's secrets, the only way to take its unrelenting attention from you is revealing something it deems more interesting than what it had to say about you. This program is looking for someone it deems as its main target, someone that did it wrong in the past, a foundation employee, a researcher, or guard, or another D-class(Purposefully kept unclear), and the information it deems interesting is something it can use to blackmail someone that gets it closer to its target. The program is in a way the reincarnation of a foundation employee, most likely a D-class killed in an experiment accident where there is no clear cut case as to who is the real culprit.

Central Narrative: The SCP speaks in a child-like manner and is single-minded in getting what it wants, it initially only communicates its blackmail secrets by going, "Did you know that X did Y on the thursday night of winter[And adds more very specific details, so that the current victim knows it knows something it shouldn't] The scp doesn't have perfect information, but is able to tell what the victim wants to keep secret the most, or the top-5, top-10 things they want to keep secret, that rarely is the information it -wants- so it uses that as a means to an end.

Hook: The goal of the scp is somewhat of a mistery up until the middle of the conversation logs, so that would keep the reader guessing what is it that it wants, the fact that it wants something specific is made clear from the beginning of the article.

item.title: Work In Progress
item.description: Odd idea I had while righting a paper.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A completely normal boring rock. The descriptions of it's physical and chemical properties is long and oddly specific (as in how it reacts to the chemical composition of an apple both combined and separated). All research on it is a cognitohazard, which causes and obsession with furthering it's research, usually until death. It is used as a punishment for found spies and deserters.

Central Narrative: When I say oddly specific, I mean there are numerous researchers who meet their end when they test how it reacts to a researcher's various bits of flesh, blood, and bone. The research is not left off site. It doesn't make the researchers hide it, nor does it make them try to share it. It only makes them keep researching. The reader is a found spy or deserter, who was sent to this anomaly to disappear.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is going to sound cliché, but O5 does not have clearance on this. The reasoning is because if they read the article, they would be affected. There may be a note from an O5 member near the bottom, where they talk about how even they fear it. It is an anomaly that they cannot know, that they know absolutely nothing about. Then it will open up into the anomalous properties as the twist.

Additional Notes: This is my 4th attempt after taking a couple months off. If I start getting defensive, let me know. I am not the best at taking criticism when I first see it. Also note that I first thought of this idea like 3 hours ago, and I wanted to get it down before I went to bed.

item.title: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Readers will be intrigued by the extensive worldbuilding of the SCPs and their backstories, as well as interesting characters. They will want to find out what will happen to the Forge and the three aliens, and how the story will end. No matter whose side they're on, the story will grip them, pulling them in, compelling them to see this story to the end. Best of all, this whole narrative is neatly packaged into the clinical tone the wiki's readers know and love!

Additional Notes: I would like to hear your thoughts, suggestions, and critiques on the narrative aspect of my SCP article

item.title: The Idol, seeking greenlight
item.description: Basically this is an object that can easily create well intentioned followers and spawn cults and religions
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tale

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout with a timeline of events addendum. Possible diary addendum for the tale.

Elevator Pitch: A little statue, that attracts people and creates a sense of purpose and community in people by altering their perception. Closeness to it gives peace and a general sense of wellbeing, distance causes a general sense of slight illness. Those feelings can be strong, but are perfectly manageable.

+ Central Narrative Hook and Notes
-collapse

Central Narrative: The core idea perhaps isn't too original, but I was more interested in how it would affects groups of people. How they would organize themselves if they all want to be as close as possible to the statue but at the same time know that in its presence they won't notice their hunger and tiredness and so they might kill themselves. Furthermore they know that they won't be allowed to keep the statue, there are those who will come to take it away, to contain it. So how they plan for it.
And I also try t explore a bit how people who are not exposed to the statue react to it. Sure, the organization tries to contain it, but there might be others who see it as an opportunity.
So beside the basic structure I would present a timeline of the events that led to the capture of the object, and a story in the first person about an attempt to steal it in order to expose a whole SCP facility.
I think presenting it as an addendum works better for one narrative, while presenting it as a story works better for a different narrative.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Rather than just the danger posed by the anomalous properties themselves I was interested in how the existence of those anomalous properties represent a thought hazard in those who know of them.

Additional Notes: I already wrote it and put it on my sandbox, mostly because I was interested in the idea and wanted to expand it, I would like some feedback and I would like to see if other people would enjoy it a much. It's mostly complete, but there are some things that can change based on feedback.
For instance in my original draft the timeline was more detailed and longer, then I streamlined it to the essentials, but I can expand it again if there's interest in it.

item.title: SCP-XXXX: A Perfect Suburban Family
item.description: Just a normal family, or is it? Maybe.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: Completely normal family and Suburban house, or so it would seem. Somewhat self-containing, but regularly monitored. Strange sightings and initial anomalous properties such as extreme temperature.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation caught wind of the supposed SCP due to a 911 call. As Foundation Agents further investigate the home and family they give contradictory reports. Initial reports show evidence that the home and entities residing in it exhibit anomalous properties. Further reports however state that there is nothing anomalous, and the Agents themselves suddenly become increasingly adamant that everything is perfectly normal and dismiss their own initial evidence which proved otherwise. A field test is done and Agents participating in it conduct separate investigations. All initial investigations during the field test turn up similar evidence of anomalous behavior. Further investigations done by the same agents show no evidence of anomalous behavior, as well as the Agents confidently stating that everything is normal. Foundation scientists theorize the home and family may be connected somehow, maybe even being one single entity that tries to keep up its own veil of normality around it for unknown reasons. Initial investigations turn up evidence of an anomaly, but later investigations do not as the SCP "fixes" evidence of its anomalous properties so it doesn't show up again for individual investigators. Individuals investigating are also affected by this "fix." The anomalous effects most likely apply individually. This theory is accepted and the home and family are classified as SCP-XXXX. Anyone investigating or documenting the SCP must work on it only once, and immediately report their findings. All initial evidence has been shown individually and only once to O5-██, O5-██, and the Ethics Committee for confirmation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Is this a misunderstanding and the SCP Foundation is investigating a normal family, or is something else going on here?

Additional Notes:

The SCP procedure of "only work on it once" gets implemented later for the documentation part, due to changes to the SCP document made by affected individuals (possible gimmick I'm thinking about) Furthermore, in the article itself it won't be as obvious that the home and family really are an SCP.

I'm mainly looking for constructive criticism. I'm basically just throwing the idea out there which is why it's plain and basic at this stage, and somewhat confusing.

item.title: Corpse of a Dead God
item.description: This is a redone version of a previous idea thread I had. This is about the mummified corpse of an animalistic humanoid.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, History

Page Layout: Containment procedure, description, tests, interview, personal report, final addendum.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a mummified body with a human torso, arms, and head, but it has animalistic legs, a tail, and horns. The mouth and eyelids are closed. It is completely unresponsive to people and could be easily written off as being dead. It has been reported to been speaking Doric Greek, Latin, and a third unknown language. It will never move and is quiet limp, but the body itself will never wither or fall apart, remaining perfectly intact. Flora will emerge in the surrounding area and will continue to grow, and if a dissection is attempted its mouth will snap open and a loud, ear-bleeding scream will emerge from it for a small period of time.

Central Narrative: (From a diary) The body was discovered in a hidden grotto on the island of Paxi in the 1950s. It was bought by the Brazilian ceo of a food processing company, who had a fascination with occult symbols and strange artifacts. The body was accidentally delivered to his hotel room near a deforested site. The next day, the sight was completely regrown. After some more "experiments" he concluded that this body could restore the earth's lost flora and fauna. But instead of using it as a way to fix deforestation, he used it to essentially create infinite resources for his own profit. He saw nothing wrong with this, claiming that if the body didn't want him to prosper, it wouldn't regrow the wild. It came as no surprise by his blue collar workers (who thought he was a witch) when he and the body disappeared, and soon his colleagues and some workers.
The foundation was soon reported and contained the corpse. It unfortunately destroyed its original containment cell and caused the causality of one personal, so it had to be moved to its own site in the end.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't believe there's any SCP quiet like this. It's a mummified corpse that's really a powerful being trapped in pathetically useless body but can still use all of its powers is a literary contradiction but a narratively important one. It explores an interesting side of big business, about how often times they try to mask their destructive actions against nature with claims of the corporation being safe and loving nature and whatnot.

Additional Notes: Of course I'll expand on pretty much everything on my draft.

item.title: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: Cheerleader Pom Poms that make everybody near you happy.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a pair of Pom Poms each having identical red, white, and blue stripes they don't display any signs of considerable wear. When a human holds SCP-XXXX, hereafter designed SCP-XXXX-1, will have their memories erased that caused them strong euphoria, this process can take only a few minutes or hours depending on the number of memories. When SCP-XXXX-1 has no more memories that can be extracted they will start to emit waves, when these waves contact a human will cause an immediate euphoria, the amount of euphoria, the length of the waves, and how long they experience euphoria is dependent on how many memories were erased to SCP-XXXX-1.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of the recordings of a Webcam taking place in a high school with two sisters named Lyvia, and Emily. All recordings were made by Lyvia until the last recording. The first recording shows the discovery of SCP-XXXX when they join a cheerleading club. Over time the recordings show the increasing depression of Emily.Almost all of the recordings show the parents of Emily and Lyvia being filled with happiness ignoring the well-being of Emily this resulted in Emily isolating herself to a nearby lake. The last recording shows Emily facing a lake repeating these questions: Who are they? Where am I? Why can't I feel anything? Why is everybody so happy?. This recording lasts until a faint sound of a splash due to the webcam being water damaged though the memory chip was unaffected.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The primary hook of this article is the way it shows how it affects SCP-XXXX-1, and the people near them. As people read the recordings they will feel more attached once it shows the connection between Emily with her family. The Pom Poms are based on a simple concept(Pom Poms that make you sadder, and make people near you happier)but gets more tragic when it goes more in-depth on its discovery.

Additional Notes: If somebody could show me a better way to explain the happy waves that would be splendid!

item.title: SCP-5127
item.content:encoded:
Spelling must be corrected.

The scroll it uses to write everything could use some better explanation.

While there are many good short SCPs, this one seems to need much more (and better) detail for it to be interesting.

Some sort of image (or at least a very detailed description) of the statue would definitely help a lot.

Overall, this SCP is very forgettable, uninteresting and honestly kinda painful to watch. There is some potential here if you elaborate on just how this statue came to be, how it acquired its knowledge, etc. You could even add a little "hook" to this if you made it so that Anubis ACCURATELY wrote down history, even when it is impossible to know what happened or even when records are contradictory.

You have a lot of work to do if you wish to make this a good SCP. It gave me the impression this is an unfinished work.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Regretful Slide Projector
item.description: First time poster, seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
First time poster, seeking greenlight for an SCP regarding a set of Kodack carousel slide projectors that synchronously display a cognitohazardous set of images.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. Also, please mind the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page layout.

Elevator Pitch: A set of Kodak carousel slide projectors that synchronously display a cognitohazardous set of images.

+ Central Narrative
- hide Central Narrative

Central Narrative: The SCP is a set of four Kodak carousel slide projectors that, despite not sharing any physical linkage, move through their slides in sync with each other. It requires no power and retains its anomalous properties even when disassembled.

The SCP stays inactive for a period of 72 hours, and turns on for 35 minutes, cycling through a set of 450 slides, despite each projector only being capable of holding 140 slides.

The first 15 slides are what are assumed to be testing slides, and display no anomalous effects. The next set of 185 slides appears differently to each observer, and are personalized, latching onto observers' subconscious anxieties and fears. Besides this, this set has the cognitohazardous quality of being impossible to walk away from — once the first slide in the set is seen, the observer cannot look away from it on their own.

If any one of the observers carries with them regret involving a dead loved one, the SCP moves onto the next set of slides. If not, then the slides end early and it goes back into its 72-hour dormant stage, ending the cognitohazardous effect.

Only observers with regret deemed significant enough by the SCP will be held on to by the cognitohazardous effect, still unable to look away. It is assumed that what is projected is a set of instructions detailing the construction of a SCP-XXXX-02, a coffin-like chamber. An observer who finishes watching the slideshow through will become obsessed with constructing this chamber, and will use every tool in their disposal in order to do so. Once they finish construction, they will attempt to obtain any remains of their dead loved ones, and enter the chamber with them. The chamber then attempts to combine the two things that enter, breaking after one use. As the only subjects tested have been D-Classes with minimal construction knowledge, their chambers were constructed shoddily and resulted in poor amalgamations.

To all other observers, the projectors appear to be projecting only white. It is unknown what exactly the schematics are, as the chamber completely deconstructs and the materials requested by the D-Class seem to disappear off of recordings and logs once the chamber expires.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I always find SCPs involving twists on normal objects interesting, and old-school slide projectors pop up in horror more than you'd think, so it seemed a good fit.

Additional Notes: N/A

item.title: Fangirl based SCP (Greenlight, please?)
item.description: Don't kill me, please.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, History, Absurdism.

Page Layout (Optional): The page have would be divided in five sections:

  1. Secure Procedures
  2. Description
  3. Acquisition
  4. "Operation Maury" (more below)
  5. Crosstestings (more below)

Elevator Pitch: As a SCP from Site-17 gave birth under unknown circumstances, researchers try to understand the new entity and, at the same time, discover who is it's father.

Central Narrative: The SCP was born when an female SCP regurgitated an egg. As the new SCP ratches from the egg, it already looks like a seven years old girl. the Scientists put it under a DNA testing that proved their parentage with the female SCP. They also discover that the new SCP has some anomalies: an “Hume normalization area” around it, acting like a SRA, and was born with innate knowledge, including Foundation’s classified information.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP has three very strange anomalies as 1) it haves a father within Site-17 (thus the "Operation Maury"), 2) it is a living SRA (so it needs some crosstesting to discover if it can be turned into a Thaumiel) and 3) it knows lots of classified information and seems to be resistant to amnestics.

Additional Notes: Somethings I want to clarify two things about this SCP:

  1. It was created based on “fangirl SCP media”, as shippings between SCPs, jokes about the “Mary Sue” concept, head canons and “fanfics”. I’ve seen that this can be a problem, but is what came to my mind when I’ve created it.
  2. I’ve already thought about dividing it, creating two SCP from it.

item.title: SCP Idea: Dynaroo
item.description: A strong Kangaroo attacks the Foundation
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A large, angry, and buff kangaroo with a personal grudge against the SCP Foundation goes from an amusing anomaly to becoming a terrifying threat.

Narrative/Hook +
Narrative/Hook -

Central Narrative: The Foundation receives reports of a very large Kangaroo ambushing D-class transports and holding facilities in Australia. Attempts to capture the Kangaroo fail as it only appears to free D-class and kill Foundation staff before disappearing, and it won’t fall for set-ups or traps. Staff’s first response is amusement at the idea of their "Looney Tunes"-esque rivalry. However, by the end, that’s contrasted by a video-log transcript where staff on a D-class transport bus are terrified at the sight of it on the horizon, coming for them.

After 2 years of failure to contain him, the Kangaroo is suddenly found in the wild and is easily captured. When the head researcher appears on-site to see the contained SCP from an observation booth, the Kangaroo assassinates the doctor with a powerful kick that kills him, the nearby staff, and destroys the containment chamber. He escapes, revealing he let the Foundation capture him in order to kill the researcher in charge of his containment.

They then discover that a D-class that escaped years ago left a record of his time in the Australian outback while on the run. After punching him out of fear, the D-class begins to bond with a rogue male Kangaroo. Over several weeks, the D-class and the Kangaroo become close companions. After a night of realizing his inevitable doom, the D-class told the Kangaroo all the secrets he knew about the Foundation as a small way to rebel against the unbeatable odds. He was eventually found and terminated by Agents who neglected to terminate the lone witness, the Kangaroo.

The Agents involved are discovered to be MIA and the same researcher who approved the termination is revealed to be the same one who became the head researcher that was assassinated. The Foundation theorizes that either the researcher was simply too careless to make the connection, or something/someone else knew and was assisting the Kangaroo in his quest for revenge.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The absurdity will make you laugh, but by emphasizing the reality of the physical strength in actual kangaroos will this SCP make you terrified. By slowly escalating the serious tone of the article, the reader realizes along with the Foundation how much they underestimated this anomaly.


Additional Notes: There will be no references to the 2003 film “Kangaroo Jack” in the article whatsoever.

Promise.

-Edited to reflect comments from IRC

This SCP aims to somewhat alleviate that. A series of instructions, warnings, one-time-use spells, etc, etc given to the victims of these anomalous incidents (just a portion of them, enough to catch the Foundation's attention) to help them escape the situation unharmed. but the reality is often bleaker than it looks.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: We are presented with the SCP, the set of requirements for its manifestation. Then, we look through the list of incidents it took place in (about 8 ~ 15 I haven't found the goldilocks number to form a pattern or a narrative yet, officially in the record, it would be around a few thousand). The pattern we see here would be that this SCP has pretty much about 35% success rate with success being the receiver will have no other connection with the anomaly and survive(of course) the rest would be either dead (anomalously or not), sunk deeper into the abnormal, recruited by different GOIs (including the Foundation). Then we are presented with some transcript of the SCP's instruction and we would see some changes in tones, sadder, more pessimistic, although more professional, a stand out transcript would show why it did what it did.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The audience would be hooked (hopefully) with the question of "What about the average civilian in the world dwelled within the anomaly?" and the methods that this unknown force behind the SCP utilizes to help the victims and how the Foundation apply them to standard protocols. Then, hopefully, the audience would see how this kind of work affects an individual, people become more jaded but also more proficient at what they do.

Additional Notes: This SCP might be a more primitive + anomalous version of 911 operatives (now I've just realized that…) but instead of you finding their help, they will try to help you. item.title: Seeking greenlights for SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I plan on adding pictures.

Elevator Pitch:

+ Open
- Close

SCP-XXXX is an event that takes place in the Netherlands on every first Monday of a month, at 12:00 CET. The following phases of SCP-XXXX then take place. These are:

1) A siren, measured about 104 decibel, sounds for 90 seconds. This siren sounds within the borders of the Netherlands from an unknown source.

2) During those 90 seconds, three Heinkel He 111 warplanes appear in the air and fly a route of 10 kilometre. The spawn location and route of these planes are random. A Vickers 7.5 tl antiaircraft cannon with crew will also appear about 7 kilometre in on that route. These planes are like an illusion in the air.

3) About 70 seconds in, the planes come into the cannon its range. The crew fires at the planes and hits one of them. The plane crashes into the cannon, making a dust cloud. You are unable to see the cannon and the crew.

4) At the end of the 90 seconds, the cannon, crew and planes disappear.

Described in one sentence it is basically: ´A monthly illusion where you follow the story of a crew shooting at three planes and you can interact with it´.

Central Narrative:
You follow a crew of five soldiers and a sergeant. During the 70 seconds prior to the shooting, during preparations, they involve in conversations letting you know more about them. They talk about the war and the sergeant in particular about his family, and how he is hoping to see they are alright. Then they get alarmed by the upcoming planes, and the crew dies to the crash.

You can interact with the crew members. There are 2 outcomes:
1. You are a civilian, they say you should go home.
2. Or you fool them by pretending to be a soldier, in that case you become part of the play (you start behaving like a soldier, no communication with you is then possible). You disappear just like the crew afterwards.

The people seeing the SCP don't pay attention to it (think it's normal) because of its effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The interesting parts where I want to focus on are the story from the crew and sergeant and what happens when you become part of the play.

Additional Notes:
1. I might have to make the time longer.
2. Yes, the siren is an actual thing in the Netherlands. I figured it could be a potential idea for an SCP.

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

Central Narrative: SCP-#### would be discovered by a field agent accidentally, when a little boy hugging the object was run over by a truck and suffered no damage at all. He (the field agent) would keep an eye on the boy for some months, who seemed to have no anomalous properties. The field agent would become a friend of the boy and his plushie. Months later, the boy would give the plushie to the field agent and make him promise to take care of “him”. He said that he would go to a place called “Imagination” and promised he would send letters to the plushie and to the agent every few weeks. The boy later would be found dead at the roadside, but the letters would keep coming. SCP-#### would be brought home by the field agent, who, when, in tears, hugged the object, would hear a voice calming him down. He would later survive a stray bullet with no damage at all while he slept, hugging the plushie. After that, the field agent would bring the object to the foundation site immediately.

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This artifact would be kept in a room safe from external groups of interest, only reliable personnel would come into contact with it and SCP-#### would sometimes ask to the ones hugging him to write letters destined to “Imagination”, saying he moved and was being treated well by the Researchers. It would be an object protected by the Foundation against some Groups of Interest, who would want to have SCP-#### so they could become invincible.

item.title: The Dark Lantern
item.description: A creature that turns you into a tree.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action, History

Elevator Pitch: A tall humanoid creature that has 2 luminous white eyes and 2 horn-like appendages resembling those of the Cervidae family. A small clothing piece seems to be covering the creature's upper part of the body and it has also been seen carrying a lantern with it. This creature manifests in any remote forested area in which humans pass. Once it manifests, it will then attempt to separate individuals from each other (if the individual is not already alone) by singing a song . The song is cognitohazardous, but it has a short range. Each individual hearing it will be tempted to follow the source of the song until it stops. Once that happens, they will be lost in the forest in which they are located with no knowledge of how they got there or how to go back. From this stage, most people make it back to society. Those who don't (cell phones and compasses won’t work) will begin to experience fatigue and illness after 1-2 days from being lost. After that, individuals will be incapable of walking or staying conscious. In the last stage, roots will begin to grow from and around these individuals. They will also begin to cough leaves as they grow inside them. Branches will also grow from their body. Slowly, they will be completely covered in wood until their original body becomes a tree. After that, SCP-XXXX will approach the tree and cut it down. It will then pick up some of the wood and put it in its lantern to keep it lit.

Central Narrative: Interviews with the creature (it is sapient and capable of speech) and history of its manifestations. It has been around for a long time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature manifestations appear in a very specific part of the year, October 31th up to November 31th. It is theorized that it can teleport, but this
hasn't been confirmed. (Spoiler) The lantern that it carries contains its soul, it must keep it lit in order to survive. That’s why it needs wood. Normal wood doesn’t seem to work in keeping it lit.

Additional Notes: I don't really have anything to say, but I hope you like the concept. I can explain the idea in more detail if there are some things that are unclear!

item.title: suadeant (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A symbiotic, disembodied voice which can be very... suggestive.
item.content:encoded:
Hello! This is my first attempt to get reviewed on anything so forgive me if it's not quite the correct format!

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (paradoxical)

Elevator Pitch: So it is thought to be a telepathic entity as the "voice" is never recorded, though it is "heard". Sometimes it is "seen" however, witness accounts differ so much it is not clear whether there are multiple entities, it changes appearance, or the witnesses are subject to a form of hysteria "if you stare into a dark room ling enough, you will eventually see something"

My thought is that the entity gets some form of nourishment by it's host acting counter to their normal behavior and it is even more valuable if the host doesn't acknowledge the entity's existance at all. Denial of its existance is good, but not as good as complete ignorance.

Central Narrative: It needs to be visited each day and the subject must remain with the entity long enough to confirm that it is in fact still contained. There is a real danger of the entity escaping sue to its nature of wanting to be forgotten, and it may have been once or twice and had it's containment treated as an "empty" chamber, allowing it to escape.

To contain, the entity will be visited by a subject each day.
The subject will be given a myriad of monotonous tasks to be completed with a large amount of inocuous restrictions placed on them. The reasoning is to give the entity a large amount of non-dangerous things to tempt the subject with and avoid another D-508905 incident.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: "something that thrives by convincing it's host that it does not exist."

Additional Notes: I figure that it will operate within the confines of suggestions available. Starting off small, but desiring a much larger payoff when available. Biding it's time while it "grooms" it's host into more severe self-contradictions.

I imagine Euclid for it's classification.

Please tell me what you think :) i hope i can start being a real contributer soon! ^^

item.title: SCP-XXXX: Empathic Erhu (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy
item.content:encoded:
A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy, and the ethical/philosophical conflicts within the Foundation that result from it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mythological, Philosophical

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout with some tests and a few cross-tests

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an emotokinetic1 erhu that when played causes anyone who hears it to receive all of the emotions and underlying memories of the player.
  • SCP-XXXX achieves this "instantaneous empathy" by generating empathons, the elementary subatomic particle of the psychospace responsible for human emotion.2
  • SCP-XXXX can transmit any human emotion, resulting in a conflict between the O5 Council and the Ethics Committee concerning how best to use SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is hand-delivered to the Foundation by the headless god of perseverance Xíng Tiān, who says that it will help humanity by bringing individuals together. Testing reveals that SCP-XXXX does this by using empathons to broadcast the emotions of the person playing SCP-XXXX.

+ show block
– hide block

However, because SCP-XXXX can use empathons to transmit any human emotion, a conflict arises between the O-5 Council, who want to weaponize SCP-XXXX, and the Ethics Committee, who want to use SCP-XXXX as a mode of communication with sapient SCP's.

This conflict is resolved when Xíng Tiān hijacks SCP-XXXX and gives all the D-class at Site-64 the ability to emotokinetically communicate with each other, allowing them to cooperate and pool their knowledge of certain SCP's to coordinate a prison break that leads to the loss of several SCP personnel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous musical instrument that generates instantaneous empathy, and this emotokinetic ability results in an ethical conflict within the Foundation. SCP-XXXX also expands upon the lore of the psychospace and certain humanoid SCP's such as SCP-5027 and SCP-5278.

Additional Notes:

  • I know that Series I SCP's like SCP-187 and SCP-682 are fairly overdone; I would be happy to substitute them for more recent SCP's. Essentially, I need an SCP with precognitive abilities and an SCP that's physically invincible.
  • I read SCP-5027 a few weeks ago and loved the premise, although I did get bummed out by the ending. If the author of SCP-5027 is okay with it, I would like to use SCP-XXXX to give SCP-5027 a somewhat happier ending (nothing like leaving containment, but at least an ending where SCP-5027 can be treated like a human being).
  • Lastly, thank you for reading this SCP idea! Any guidance is much appreciated, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Collapsible edited as the post was still rather long. ~Zyn

Footnotes
1. capable of controlling the emotions of sentient beings
2. similar to the Higgs Boson being responsible for mass or the photon being responsible for light

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Unsolved Hypercube
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Rubik's cube which, when close to being solved, begins to behave like a 4-dimensional Rubik's cube to prevent itself from being solved. When it nears being solved again it will instead begin to behave like a 5-dimensional Rubik's cube, and so on. After being far away enough from being solved it will revert to a lower dimension. These processes have a consistent order and pattern. As a byproduct SCP-XXXXs mass increases with each dimension over 3 dimensions it contains (starting with the mass of a regular Rubik's cube) as well as giving off a small amount of ionizing radiation. This increase in mass and the presence of radiation grows exponentially with each additional dimension.

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of several testing logs where Dr. Cass experiments with SCP-XXXX and its unusual properties. Over time they work towards the possibility of using SCP-XXXXs radioactive properties for fuel in a power generator based on fusion reactor designs. This pursuit eventually leads to conflict with the site director who is against the idea. By the end of it the site director removes Dr. Cass as the project lead (instead having them as a project advisor) and further experimentation with SCP-XXXX is delayed until a new project lead can be established.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The primary hook of this article is the mundane appearance of the anomaly in question. As people read it some might look at a Rubik’s cube they have (or a memory of it) which can draw them in closer. It's also a simple concept (a Rubik’s cube which prevents you from solving it) but goes very deep into the mechanics of the anomaly and such a concept actually works.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.description: A particularly dangerous MK II Toyota Supra
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): I'm planning to add, to the usual stuff, a short log of the manhunt, three interviews with the driver and a test log - in that order.

Elevator Pitch: A MK II Supra. The faster it goes, the more universally degrading/degenerative its shell becomes - to the point where it can cut clean through practically anything. As a trade-off, it loses speed proportionally to damage done.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

From the American midwest and moving south, a retired stuntman drives recklessly and attracts the police. In chases, he uses the car to his advantage - cutting through roadblocks and anything else that stands in his way. The Foundation is, of course, not very fond of this, and teams up with the FBI for a manhunt, which lasts 2 whole days and ultimately ends with a cleverly placed spike strip.

The old man is then brought in in a heavily intoxicated state, high on cocaine and MDMA. The three separate interviews are conducted within 1, 3 and 7 days inside his padded holding cell, which reveal the man's motivation to be a combination of forced retirement, an uneventful lifestyle and poverty. The straw that broke the camel's back was the death of his only friend, whose will provided him with the black-on-yellow car. Realizing his life is already lived and not going to get better, the old man is overcome by rage and sadness. In that moment, he snaps and decides to go out with a bang - by buying copious amounts of drugs and embarking on a journey to the Californian West Coast, where he had once spent the brightest days of his youth.

The old man volunteers to sacrifice himself for the sake of science in D-Class, but the Ethics Committee instead persists that he be amnesticized and provided a fake story about his car being stolen. The old man, monitored for a week after his release, ends up making friends with some of the local car enthusiasts.

While testing, the researchers perform experiments such as replacing parts with aftermarket parts, simply taping objects to it and driving it into increasingly massive obstacles. It is concluded that A) The anomaly acts at an atomic level, separating molecules into individual atoms; B) The reaction time is a negative ln-logarhythm of the car's speed; and C) That its effects become less and less intense as testing goes on. Due to the last point, experiments needed to be reduced and now require authorization from a Senior Researcher.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The stuntman as a person and various experiments performed on the car.

Additional Notes: The old man's friend knew of the anomalous properties, and kept it locked up in a rentable garage out of fear and paranoia. He first found it abandoned in front of his junkyard.
